target: Spoiler-free 100% sandbox completion of The Sims 2: Legacy Collection, all eight expansions, and all included Stuff Packs

areas.name: Legacy Route and Neighborhood Safety
areas.location_cue: The Windows launcher, neighborhood selector, expansion destinations, save folders, and content catalog.
areas.note: Chosen route: native Windows Legacy Collection with eight expansions and nine included Stuff Packs.

levels.1: Confirm the current complete Windows route before building a long-term neighborhood.
levels.2: Install and update the Legacy Collection.
levels.3: Launch the current Windows build, create a test neighborhood, and verify every expansion destination and included Stuff Pack catalog before starting the permanent completion save.

levels.1: University through Apartment Life should all be active.
levels.2: Check every expansion system and destination.
levels.3: Verify campuses, Downtown, owned businesses, pets, vacation travel, seasons, hobby enthusiasm, apartments, and witches. Stop if any system is absent.

levels.1: The current Legacy Collection does not include one historical licensed Stuff Pack.
levels.2: Exclude IKEA Home Stuff from this chosen route.
levels.3: Do not mark its objects missing. Keep the omission in the local research record and rebuild only if EA later adds the licensed pack to the collection.

levels.1: Long-running neighborhoods can suffer corruption if characters or lots are damaged.
levels.2: Back up the complete neighborhood folder before major experiments.
levels.3: Exit fully, copy the neighborhood and shared character data to a dated backup, and make new checkpoints before supernatural transformations, business restructuring, vacation travel, and family-tree edits.

save_backup.title: Back up the neighborhood first
save_backup.why: This completion route changes many households, lots, memories, and family trees over a long save.
save_backup.detail: Exit the game and copy the full neighborhood folder before beginning the permanent ledger.

save_backup.title: Back up before aspiration experiments
save_backup.why: Aspiration conversion and failed reward states can permanently alter the test Sim.
save_backup.detail: Use a separate branch before changing aspirations or deliberately testing a reward failure.

areas.name: Nightlife, Downtown, and Dating
areas.location_cue: The Downtown selector, restaurants, clubs, bowling lanes, date and outing meters, chemistry panel, matchmaker, driveways, garages, and vehicle catalog.
areas.note: Complete Downtown activities, both date extremes, a top outing, chemistry, cars, and Nightlife’s social systems.

levels.1: The nightlife district gathers several social venues in one sub-neighborhood.
levels.2: Use every distinct public activity available in Downtown.
levels.3: Visit suitable community lots and successfully dine at a staffed restaurant, bowl, sing karaoke, dance on a floor, use the DJ booth, enter the dance sphere, take a photo, and play poker.

levels.1: Following both Sims’ current wants steadily improves the shared meter.
levels.2: Finish a date at the highest score tier.
levels.3: Invite a compatible partner, choose a lot with useful social and fun objects, fulfill wants for both Sims, avoid fears and interruptions, and end only after the meter reaches Dream Date.

levels.1: Use a disposable backup branch for the opposite end of the meter.
levels.2: Finish one date at the bottom score tier.
levels.3: Back up first, begin a date with a test household, repeatedly trigger the displayed fears or rejected interactions until the meter reaches Horrible, let the date end, record the result, then restore the clean save.

levels.1: A coordinated group responds well to shared activities and fulfilled social wants.
levels.2: End an outing at its highest rating.
levels.3: Form a group, invite every member to a well-equipped community lot, keep the party together, rotate through activities everyone can join, fulfill group wants, and remain until the outing meter reaches its top tier.

levels.1: Aspiration, personality, and attraction settings determine romantic compatibility.
levels.2: Create a pair whose relationship panel shows three chemistry bolts.
levels.3: Choose compatible aspirations and personalities, adjust each Sim’s two turn-ons and one turn-off, use the room-scoping interaction to confirm attraction, and refine the settings until three bolts appear.

levels.1: A larger fee improves the chance of a compatible introduction.
levels.2: Pay the matchmaker for her strongest blind-date attempt.
levels.3: Call or meet the matchmaker, select the blind-date service, pay the maximum available amount, complete the introduced date, and record the resulting chemistry and score.

items.label: Own and Drive Every Car Model

levels.1: Residential driveways open a small finite vehicle catalog.
levels.2: Purchase and drive all five Nightlife car models.
levels.3: Build a driveway or garage, buy each distinct model in turn, assign an owner, drive it to a community lot and back, then retain a catalog record before selling or replacing it.

levels.1: Two Nightlife objects allow controlled changes to attraction and aspiration settings.
levels.2: Test the portable attraction adjuster and the aspiration-changing reward.
levels.3: Back up first, use the portable object to revise turn-ons and turn-offs, then use the aspiration reward under a safe aspiration state, verify both changes, and restore if the outcome harms the completion household.

levels.1: A severe social conflict can create a temporary hostile state.
levels.2: Cause fury on a backup branch and let it expire.
levels.3: Back up, use a test pair to provoke the temporary fury marker, inspect its relationship effects, wait until the state clears, record the mechanic, and restore the clean branch.

levels.1: Successful public socializing can preserve a lighter relationship link.
levels.2: Make another Sim appear as a contact.
levels.3: Socialize positively during an outing or community visit, finish the event successfully, and confirm the new contact marker or relationship benefit after returning home.

save_backup.title: Back up before negative social tests
save_backup.why: The lowest date tier and fury can damage relationships and leave unwanted memories.
save_backup.detail: Record those mechanics on a restored test branch, not in the permanent household.

areas.name: Sandbox Final Audit
areas.location_cue: Neighborhood backups, family trees, memory panels, collections, career rewards, aspiration panels, badges, vacation mementos, hobby plaques, and supernatural households.
areas.note: The game has no universal completion percentage, so these finite ledgers define the auditable route.

levels.1: Use a written neighborhood ledger because completion is distributed across many households.
levels.2: Recheck aspirations, skills, careers, degrees, businesses, pets, seasons, vacations, hobbies, apartments, life states, worlds, and catalogs.
levels.3: Load each specialist household, verify its permanent unlocks and displays, inspect every relevant panel, and retain a master index linking each requirement to the household that completed it.

levels.1: Preserve the final state before continuing ordinary generational play.
levels.2: Create a read-only copy of the full completed save tree.
levels.3: Exit the game, copy all completed neighborhoods and shared data to dated storage, verify the archive size, and keep a separate writable copy for future play.

levels.1: Expansion and Stuff Pack catalogs contain many unique mechanics beyond decoration.
levels.2: Use each object with a distinct interaction or unlock at least once.
